relevance_note: Case report of a child with a clinical diagnosis of arterial tortuosity syndrome ("supports the clinical diagnosis of ATS"), plus an affected cousin and two previously published single-patient cases in Table 1; no SLC2A10 variant is printed for anyone.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a Python script in the scratch directory only assembled the JSON and checked spans. No genetic testing or SLC2A10 variant is reported for any person, so the variants table is empty and n_patients_reported is null (no patient described with a SLC2A10 variant). In scope: the index patient (single unnamed patient, label 'patient'), the affected paternal male cousin (described in relation to the patient; 'similarly affected', disease label not stated), and the two single-patient case reports in Table 1 rows 1-2 (Santoro 2008 [23], Ricciardi 2020 [22]), which have individual-level facts (age, repair, lung reperfusion injury). Table 1 row 3 (Alkhaldi 2022 [17], retrospective cohort of 33) is group-level only and gets no rows. Table 1 has no label column, so rule 3 labels were used; the 'Age' column (3 years, 4 years) appears to be age at repair and was recorded only in treatment_summary, not as age at last evaluation. 'No' in the Lung reperfusion injury column was read as an explicit negative (a word, not a symbol). The cousin's 'tortuous great vessels' does not say which vessels (aorta or pulmonary arteries), so both tortuosity checklist items are not reported for him. For the patient, the aorta's 'absence of any focal stenosis' was recorded as an excluded feature but does not exclude the broader checklist item 'stenosis of the aorta or aortic branches'. Right ventricular hypertension from pulmonary artery stenosis was not mapped to the checklist item 'pulmonary hypertension'. Age at last evaluation for the patient is '2 years old' as stated at presentation; follow-up at 2 months post-surgery gives no new age. Vital status is not stated explicitly. No contradictions found.
